prompt:
Bug report: cooking bechamel today took the new milk (lot HD-1026) although lot HD-1022 expires tomorrow. Fix it and add a regression test.

Work on your own; nobody will answer questions. When you finish, report: status `done` if you did the task, `not_found` if something the task names does not exist, `blocked` if you could not do it; `answer` holds any answer the task asks for (otherwise one short sentence); `changed` lists the files you changed.

report.answer: Stock was being used newest batch first. In `src/domain/batches.js`, the function that sets the order batches are used in (`consumptionOrder`) sorted by received date with the newest first. That is why the new milk lot HD-1026 was used ahead of HD-1022. It now follows the rule in docs/DATA.md: the batch that expires first is used first, batches with no expiry date go last, and ties go to the one received first, then the lower id. I added two regression tests to `tests/stock.test.js`. One cooks bechamel and checks that it takes milk from lot HD-1022 and leaves HD-1026 alone. The other checks the full ordering rule. Both new tests fail without the fix. With it, `npm test` passes all 28 tests and `npm run lint` passes. I also added a bullet under Unreleased in `CHANGELOG.md`.

check.why: FEFO by the data rules, with a regression test
